column1: # cpython_known_bugs.tsv — regression catalog for the cpython-review-toolkit `known-issues` command.
# GENERATED by scripts/gen_known_bugs.py from reports/*/meta.json — do NOT hand-edit.
# The canonical source of truth is each finding's meta.json.
#   bug_id     upstream issue (gh-NNNNNN) when filed, else the findings-repo id (CPY-####)
#   path       repo-relative CPython C source path
#   line       1-indexed line, or 0 if unknown (match by function/category)
#   category   recursion | pyerr-clear | uninit-dealloc | null-deref | refcount | tsan
#   function   enclosing function (for line-drift-tolerant matching), or 0 if unknown
# NOTE: some crash shapes carry no scannable token at the exact site (a native
# stack overflow, a data race). For those, `absent` against a fresh scan is NOT
# proof of a fix — read the file. See the `known-issues` command docs.

column6: note
PyObject_GC_NewVar(PyStructSequence, type, size) where size = REAL_SIZE_TP(type) is read from the type's Python-writable n_fields; _PyObject_VAR_SIZE multiplies unchecked
for (i = 0; i < size; i++) obj->ob_item[i] = NULL - the same unbounded size also drives the zero-fill loop
res->ob_item[i] = Py_NewRef(v) - the observed out-of-bounds WRITE of size 8 into the undersized region
for (i = len; i < max_len; ++i) - the unclamped loop bound; only entered when the optional dict argument is non-empty (guard at :238)
const char *name = type->tp_members[i - n_unnamed_fields].name - out-of-bounds READ; the loop bound max_len is the type's Python-writable n_fields while tp_members is a fixed C array
PyDict_GetItemStringRef(dict, name, &ob) hands the garbage name to PyUnicode_FromString -> strlen; the observed crash frame
same shape on the `error:` label, reached from either _PyStaticType_InitBuiltin or initialize_structseq_dict failing

PyMem_Free(members) after initialize_static_fields set type->tp_members = members (:592) and initialize_static_type ran PyType_Ready, which created one PyMemberDescr per entry holding a d_member pointer into the array
the public void wrapper is `(void)PyStructSequence_InitType2(...)` - it discards the failure code, so an extension using this spelling hands out the dangling type instead of bailing out
Py_DECREF(subargs) where subargs is always NULL -- tuple_extend fails only via _PyTuple_Resize, which NULLs its out-param on every failure path. Fix: delete this line.
PyErr_Format(..., type->tp_name) reads offset 0x18 through a NULL `type`; this is the faulting instruction (ASan: SEGV on unknown address 0x18)
supercheck(su->type, obj) called with no NULL check on su->type -- the entry point that reaches the fault
bytes = PyBytes_FromStringAndSize(NULL, bytes_size) with no NULL check; PyBytes_AS_STRING(bytes) at :958 dereferences it unconditionally
value = Py_NewRef(failobj) on the node-found-but-dict-pop-failed path; failobj is NULL for od.pop(key) and for popitem (:1172)
Py_SETREF(gi->obj, NULL) re-reads gi->obj after an unsynchronised NULL check at :942; the loser DECREFs NULL (or double-DECREFs the same object)
PyErr_Clear() with no PyErr_ExceptionMatches narrowing after PyObject_Hash(arg) == -1; discards ANY exception the user __hash__ raised
_PyErr_Clear(tstate) after _PySys_Audit(..."cpython.PyInterpreterState_Clear"...) < 0 -- no narrowing, no save/restore, no PyErr_WriteUnraisable

PyObject_Hash(alias->origin), unguarded. A GenericAlias chain nested through ORIGIN (types.GenericAlias(g, ())) is PURE ga_hash self-recursion -- 246 identical frames, no tuple_hash involved, so the proposed gh-154362 tuple_hash guard does NOT bound it. REPRODUCED
PyObject_Hash(alias->args), unguarded. hash(list[list[...]]) alternates ga_hash <-> tuple_hash (123 of each). REPRODUCED

self->hash = PyObject_Hash(obj) on the referent, no Py_EnterRecursiveCall. REPRODUCED on both the GIL ASan build and the free-threaded ASan build (246 alternating weakref_hash / weakref_hash_lock_held frames)

Py_BEGIN_CRITICAL_SECTION(self) wrapping the call -- the recursion happens INSIDE the critical section, so on a free-threaded build the overflow occurs with N nested per-object locks held. On the FT ASan build the faulting PC is this line, i.e. it dies entering the Nth critical section

Py_hash_t hash = PyObject_Hash(arg) on a caller-supplied union member, no Py_EnterRecursiveCall. GRADED AS AN ENTRY POINT, NOT A DESCENT: it contributes exactly ONE C frame (verified by gdb: frame #261929, with #261928 ga_hash and #261927..#0 all tuple_hash). REPRODUCED

the INCIDENTAL bound: PyObject_CallFunction(prepare, "OO", self, item) for __typing_prepare_subst__ enters the ceval recursion guard once per level, so with a real typing.TypeVar parameter the same descent degrades to a clean RecursionError ("while calling a Python object", gdb-verified at cfunction_enter_call). A duck-typed parameter with __typing_subst__ but no __typing_prepare_subst__ makes no Python call and the descent is unguarded

`PyObject *subargs = _Py_subs_parameters(self, arg, parameters, item);` -- self-recursive substitution walk over nested list/tuple args, no Py_EnterRecursiveCall. STILL UNGUARDED on upstream main after gh-154277 (verified against the GitHub contents API; the merged guard is in _Py_make_parameters only). REPRODUCED: 241 identical :482 frames under ASan, exit 139 on the plain debug build

self-recursive parameter walk, no Py_EnterRecursiveCall. REPRODUCED (247 identical :231 frames under ASan; 104,784 frames under gdb). FIXED upstream by gh-154277 (merged 2026-07-20), which added Py_EnterRecursiveCall(" in __parameter__ calculation") at the top of the function

REACHABILITY WIDENING: `alias->parameters = _Py_make_parameters(alias->args)` -- a typing.Union built with `|` drives the same walk. gdb frame #104785 sits directly under the recursion, entered from union_parameters (:367) via `u.__parameters__`. Fixed transitively by gh-154277 (the guard is inside the callee)

second Union entry point: `u[str]` -> _Py_subs_parameters. On both local binaries this route still crashes at :332 first (union_init_parameters runs before :349 and _Py_make_parameters overflows at a shallower depth -- verified by sweep: N=104000 both survive, N=106000 make_parameters already crashes). The independent _Py_subs_parameters self-recursion it leads to is recorded separately as CPY-0023 and is NOT fixed by gh-154277

PyObject_Hash(value) with no Py_EnterRecursiveCall; the function is literally commented "Code copied from tuple_hash()" and the copy carried the missing guard. REPRODUCED (ASan stack-overflow, 1M-deep frozendict, 245 alternating frames)

the _PyDict_Next loop that calls frozendict_pair_hash for every (key, value) pair -- the other half of the alternating recursion. Keys are safe: their hashes are computed and cached at insertion (entry->hash), so only VALUES recurse
PyObject_Hash(item[i]) in the element loop, no Py_EnterRecursiveCall; deep/cyclic tuple -> C-stack SIGSEGV. REPRODUCED (ASan stack-overflow, 1M-deep tuple, 246 identical frames)

entry point only: PyObject_Hash(alias->hashable_args) contributes ONE frame into tuple_hash's descent, it is not itself a recursive descent. Not independently crashable -- union construction hashes every member first (CPY-0022), so the member hashes are already memoised by the time union_hash runs
seq = it->it_seq loaded BORROWED; PySequence_GetItem(seq, ...) at :70 then runs arbitrary Python
Py_DECREF(seq) on a stale local after it->it_seq was already NULLed+dropped by a re-entrant inner next(); ASan heap-use-after-free
args = tuple_args = PySequence_Tuple(args) -- the aliasing that makes :541 free what :542 reads
PyTuple_GET_ITEM(args, iarg) read after :541 Py_XDECREF(tuple_args) freed the very tuple args aliases; result fed to PyErr_Format("%T")
`odictiterobject tmp = *di;` copies PyObject_HEAD by value, capturing a LOCKED PyMutex when reached re-entrantly from inside odictiter_iternext's critical section
PySequence_List((PyObject*)&tmp) -> odictiter_iternext(&tmp) -> Py_BEGIN_CRITICAL_SECTION(&tmp) -> PyMutex_Lock on the locked copy -> _PyParkingLot_Park with timeout_ns=-1
lazy init of op->func_annotations; safe only when the caller holds the function's critical section
Py_XSETREF(op->func_annotations, ann_dict) then `return ann_dict` BORROWED -- two threads both store, the loser's dict is DECREF'd out from under the winner's borrowed return
public C-API entry point; calls func_get_annotation_dict at :587 with NO critical section, bypassing the gh-128714 fix
reads the parameters tuple obtained from the unguarded ga_getitem:590 load while another thread is still allocating/filling it (tuple_add <- _Py_make_parameters:218)
unguarded inline lazy init of alias->parameters (read :583, raw store :584); races the critical-section-guarded write in ga_parameters_lock_held:848
unsynchronised read of descr->d_qualname in the lazy-cache check
raw store of calculate_qualname() result; no Py_XSETREF, so the loser's str leaks (+2 refs/descriptor measured)
opens with the unchecked macro _PyObject_GC_UNTRACK(di); asserts _PyObject_GC_IS_TRACKED -> abort. This is the observed crash line.
Py_DECREF(di) on the _PyTuple_FromPairSteal failure path, before kind/di_odict/di_current are written (:1960-1965) and before _PyObject_GC_TRACK (:1967)
Py_DECREF(op) on the list_allocate_array failure branch, inside #ifdef Py_GIL_DISABLED, with op->ob_item unassigned (:266) and Py_SIZE(op) unset (:275)
free_list_items(op->ob_item, false) - reached because the `op->ob_item != NULL` guard at :560 sees the debug allocator's 0xcd fill; the observed crash frame
TYPE_LIST: v = PyList_New(n) with n bounded only by SIZE32_MAX - the pure-Python reachability route via marshal.loads
while (i--) Py_XDECREF(it->parent_stack[i].parent) with i = the uninitialized it->parent_stack_used read at :2178 and parent_stack == NULL; the observed crash line
Py_DECREF(it) on the `it->parent_stack = PyMem_New(...) == NULL` branch, before parent_stack_used/parent_stack_size are set at :2381-2382
Py_CLEAR(self->stringsiter) on the uninitialized pointer; the observed crash line, reached via templateiter_dealloc:45
Py_DECREF(iter) on the PyObject_GetIter(self->strings) failure branch - same defect, one branch earlier; the line cited by upstream gh-151815
Py_DECREF(iter) on the PyObject_GetIter(self->interpolations) failure branch, before the member writes at :243-245; the branch the reproduction actually takes
Py_DECREF(di) on the _PyTuple_FromPairSteal failure path, before _PyObject_GC_TRACK(di) at :5653
untracks with the unchecked macro _PyObject_GC_UNTRACK(di); the observed crash line
